claims.text: Lisa Demuth, the Republican Minnesota House Speaker, and Sen. Amy Klobuchar held their first governor's debate on October 19, 2026.
Demuth asked Klobuchar "Why didn't you do more."
Klobuchar said "I would have caught that fraud. I would have done something about it."
Klobuchar has served in the U.S. Senate since 2006.
Klobuchar said she called the Justice Department and asked for more resources.
Demuth pledged to fire all of Minnesota's commissioners.

shorts.title: Smithsonian To Black Conservative Filmmaker: Pay $35,000 To Screen Your Film #Shorts
shorts.hook: "The right kind of Black?" - Smithsonian fight
shorts.narration: Folks, the Smithsonian says it loves diverse views. [deadpan] Terms and conditions apply. Filmmaker Eli Steele asked the National Museum of African American History and Culture for a public screening of his documentary White Guilt. Per emails Fox News reviewed, the museum said his dates were unavailable and offered a private rental at a quoted thirty-five thousand dollars. [beat] Thirty-five grand. Steele asked, quote, "Do you have to be the right kind of Black to be shown at the Smithsonian?" The museum didn't respond to Fox's request for comment. [sarcastic] Proverbs 18:13 says, "He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him." [beat] So Democrats: if your arguments are so strong, what are you scared of in a theater? Please subscribe. Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: Filmmaker Eli Steele asked the Smithsonian's National Museum of African American History and Culture to hold a public screening of his documentary White Guilt.
According to emails Steele provided to Fox News, the museum said his proposed dates were unavailable and offered a private rental at a quoted $35,000 instead of a museum-sponsored public screening.
Steele asked: "Do we have viewpoint diversity or do we not? Do you have to be the right kind of Black to be shown at the Smithsonian?"
The museum did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
The museum has previously programmed films including 13th, I Am Not Your Negro and Faith in Blackness.
